For MasterCard Purchase Repayment transactions, the merchant shall submit the Merchant Name in Segment 111 Table ID 047 (Soft Descriptor) in the format 'Installment Provider name*Merchant name'.
The Consumer Bill Payment/Purchase Repayment indicator value 'CB' shall be used only for Visa transactions, and value 'IR' shall be used only for MasterCard transactions.
The Table ID 59 country code shall identify the country in which the acquiring institution resides, consistent with the merchant/acquirer configuration.
A country reference in Table ID 59 shall use a valid three-digit country code from the Appendix AC list.
Real Time Account Updater applies only to card-not-present transactions from a participating, registered/certified acquirer/merchant that are Credential-on-File, Installment, or Recurring payments.

A participating merchant shall send the Account Updater Request Indicator (Segment 111, Table ID 060, Sub Table ID 01) as the trigger on Installment, Recurring, and Credential-on-File request messages.

An estimated authorization and its incremental authorizations expire 14 days after the initial estimated authorization for cruise/lodging/vehicle-rental merchants, or 7 days for other rental merchants, after which the merchant is subject to chargeback unless completion is initiated within that window.

An incremental authorization request shall follow an estimated/initial authorization, must not resend the estimated-authorization indicator, and must carry the same Sequence Number, Transaction Identifier, and Terminal Transaction Number (Segment 111 Table ID 63) as the original estimated/initial request.
An estimated/initial authorization request for a permitted merchant shall include the estimated authorization indicator (Acquirer Trace Data Sub Table ID 09) when the final amount is unknown.
Estimated and Incremental Authorization is permitted only for MCC 4121 and 5411 (card-not-present) and MCC 5552 (EV transactions).
TCP/IP Message Length is a two-byte length of all following message data excluding the length field itself.
TCP/IP Message Length is transmitted in network byte order with the high-order byte first.
The TPDU Protocol ID is fixed at 0x60.
TPDU destination and source address bytes are zero when sending messages to BUYPASS.
A POS purchase request identifies ATL105 and declares the serialized segment count in Data Section 1.
A POS purchase with fuel and product detail includes Product Code Segment 102 and preserves product order and delimiters.
The sum of Product Code Segment 102 product amounts agrees with the applicable Segment 100 amounts.
A POS purchase Prompt Code identifies purchase/capture transaction type 0 and the applicable card type.
A financial response associated with a Segment 100 transaction shall carry a valid two-digit Authorizer Code from ATL105 Appendix C.
The response Authorizer Code shall be consistent with the transaction/card/authorizer context when that context is known.
Authorizer codes documented by ATL105 but not production-enabled shall be held for configuration or deployment review rather than silently approved.

Each Appendix C Authorizer Code shall map to exactly one documented Authorizer Type (e.g., Credit, Debit, Fleet, EBT, Check, Stored Value/Gift, Proprietary, Loyalty, Other), and response interpretation shall be consistent with that type.
Alphabetical state codes used in Card Discretionary Block Data or state context shall use an Appendix D alphabetical code.
A non-US/non-Canada location using numeric state code 00 shall include Variable Information Table 041 country subdivision data.
Terminal Identifier Element 102 shall contain a valid two-digit ANSI state code from Appendix D in its defined terminal identity structure.
Conoco internal code 89 shall not be used as the merchant Prompt Code; merchant transactions use card type 090.
Financial Segment 100 Prompt Codes shall use one of the 36 Appendix E card types valid for financial transaction Prompt Codes.
A financial Prompt Code shall combine a valid Appendix G transaction type with a valid Appendix E financial card type.
Special three-character Prompt Codes shall be validated as special transaction artifacts and not accepted as standard financial Segment 100 Prompt Codes.
Fuel products shall precede nonfuel products, and EV fuel product data shall be first where applicable.
Product amounts shall reconcile to Segment 100 fuel, nonfuel, tax, and cash totals.
Each type of fuel purchase shall use a unique Product Code.
Product Code 000 shall not be used as a product because Appendix F identifies it as unused.
Standard financial Segment 100 requests support the 13 source-defined financial Transaction Type codes.
Lifecycle transaction types use the source-defined relationships for completion, cancellation, reversal, void, and timeout recovery.
Authorization/completion and sale/reversal lifecycle behavior shall preserve the applicable MasterCard preauthorization or final-authorization context when relevant.
Transaction Type 9 denotes a special transaction and shall not be treated as a standard financial Segment 100 request.
Visa recurring-payment decline codes K= and K# stop or prevent resubmission according to the source rule.
A response Decline Code in the Appendix H data-reentry family shall prompt the applicable clerk/customer data correction and resubmission behavior.
Decline Codes 4I and 6C identify a timed-out transaction and permit the source-defined retry/reversal handling.
Decline Code 4M identifies a TransArmor token-retrieval failure and permits the source-defined retry behavior.
When Terminal Identifier uses the Appendix D non-US/non-Canada state-code condition, Variable Information Table 041 shall carry the country subdivision data required by the source.

Sub Table 18 (Purchase Restriction Method) is mandatory on MasterCard Enhanced EMV Fleet (Product IDs MCF/MGF) Authorization, Pre-Authorization, and Completion transactions, and must not be sent for any other transaction; if omitted, Buypass defaults to Visa No Restrictions supported.
Variable Information Segment 111 shall use the Table ID defined for the applicable transaction/card/merchant context.
Variable Information Table Length and Table Data shall respect the source-defined layout and maximum length for the selected Table ID.
A Segment 100 transaction requiring Variable Information shall include Segment 111 in Data Section 3 and Element 63 shall include it in the serialized count.
POS Entry Mode Element 113 shall contain a valid two-digit PAN Entry Mode followed by a valid one-digit Terminal Capability Mode.
Entry Mode 10, 82, and terminal capability mode 3 shall be used only in their source-defined card, network, and mPOS contexts.
POS Entry Mode shall persist across lifecycle transactions except for source-defined exceptions, including PAN mode 90 referenced by a completion or void using mode 02.
PAN Entry Mode shall use a source-defined value consistent with the card-entry method and transaction context.
Terminal Capability Mode shall reflect the POS PIN, EMV, contactless, or mPOS capability hierarchy.
AVS/NVS Additional Information Table ID 003 shall use the source-defined signed response representation and issuer response code.
Balance Information Table ID 001 shall use its source-defined fixed layout when a financial response returns balance data.
Card Verification Additional Information shall use the source-defined Table ID 004 layout when the response returns CVV/CVC/CID/DTVV results.
A financial response shall set the Additional Information Data Segment Flag consistently with whether Segment 118 follows.
Additional Information Segment 118 shall use a valid Appendix K Table ID, length, and maximum data layout.
Currency Code usage shall be consistent with the applicable Visa, MasterCard, or both-card-network designation.
A currency value used by a Segment 100 transaction context shall use a valid three-digit Appendix L Currency Code.
Currency subfields in eWIC WIC Discount Amount and related variable data shall use a valid Appendix L code.
HIP purchase/return program data shall use the source-defined account type, amount type, currency, descriptor, and zero-filled amount detail.
Element 164 shall support multiple valid program-data subelements with a total length covering all subelements.
Each EBT Program Data subelement shall contain a valid tag, length, and detail payload whose length matches the declared length.
EBT Program Data Element 164 shall begin with a three-digit zero-filled total length matching all following program-data characters.
The Track II PVKI field is not currently used by the First Data Premium Gift Card system and shall not be validated as a meaningful business value.
The Track II Start Sentinel and End Sentinel characters shall be cut from the packet and shall not appear in the data transmitted to the host application.

The Account Number field used for serial-number derivation shall decompose into a 6-byte BIN, a 9-byte Partial Account Number, and a 1-byte Visa modulo check digit, totaling the 16-digit Account Number.
Premium Gift Card serial-number derivation shall use the source-defined BIN, partial account, check digit, and discretionary-data components when the flow requires it.
Premium Gift Card Track II data shall contain a 16-digit Account Number using the assigned Premium Gift Card BIN structure.
Premium Gift Card Track II data shall preserve the source-defined separator, YYMM expiration, service code, PVV, discretionary data, and integrity characters.
In-App token cryptogram data shall use the source-defined 28-byte or 56-byte base64 representation and token-data-block interpretation.
56 bytes of cryptogram data shall be interpreted as Token Data Block A followed by Token Data Block B; 28 bytes of cryptogram data shall be interpreted as Token Data Block A only.
Tokenized Segment 100 transactions shall use a POS Entry Mode that identifies the token presentment mode.
A payment token used as Segment 100 Account Number shall be a valid 13-19 digit token value subject to account validation and designated token BIN rules.
Payment Token Expiration Date shall be populated in the PAN Expiration Date field when token processing requires it.
A payment token shall pass basic account-number validation rules, including the LUHN check, and shall fall within a BIN range designated and flagged as a token BIN range.
A payment token value must not be the same value as the cardholder's actual PAN.
TransArmor administrative command responses shall be validated using the dedicated TransArmor specification rather than the standard Segment 100 financial response rules.
When a TransArmor administrative operation affects a Segment 100 tokenized transaction, its response and token state shall remain correlated with the originating transaction context.
National POS Condition Code shall contain the source-defined ten-position structure: terminal class, presentation type, security condition, and terminal type.
POS Condition Code shall be consistent with Segment 100 Prompt Code, entry mode, transaction lifecycle, and eWIC/channel context.
Presentation positions shall correctly identify customer/card presence, mail/telephone order, preauthorization, retention capability, and re-presentment state.
Security Condition position shall use valid values for no concern, suspected fraud, verified identification, or electronic commerce digital signature.
Terminal class and terminal type positions shall use valid Appendix Q values consistent with the physical or digital POS channel.
EMV Chip Data shall begin with a valid three-digit length consistent with the following encoded chip data.
EMV chip values such as authorized amount, transaction type, currency, and terminal country shall agree with the Segment 100 transaction context.
An EMV Segment 100 transaction shall include Segment 130 EMV Request Data in Data Section 3.
EMV Chip Data shall preserve valid BCD-packed/hex TLV tag, length, and value structure.
An EMV Segment 100/130 transaction shall use CA key configuration consistent with the applicable EMV AID and public-key data.
A CA Public Key file shall use the CA_KEYS file name, version, comma-separated records, and CRLF termination.
Each CA Public Key record shall contain valid expiry date, SHA-1 hash indicator, RSA algorithm indicator, RID, index, modulus, exponent, and checksum fields.
CARC Additional Information Table ID 002 shall carry the one-character Card Authentication Results Code returned by Visa.
EMV Table Data included in an authorization response shall be echoed in subsequent advice or batch-upload requests when required by the source.
EMV Additional Information Table ID 001 shall use the source-defined length and EMVYES/EMVNOT request values.
A Visa Digital Wallet transaction shall be classified as either Pass-through or Staged, and the applicable category-specific rules shall govern its processing.
A pass-through Digital Wallet Operator must ensure the cardholder consents in writing to the use of their account in the wallet before completing a transaction.
A pass-through Digital Wallet Operator must not perform Visa payment services on behalf of another Digital Wallet Operator.
A pass-through Visa Digital Wallet transaction shall preserve the supplied account/token credential and identify the applicable tokenized presentment context.
Purchase and Funding stages shall retain their individual transaction identity while preserving the wallet relationship and applicable lifecycle references.
A staged digital wallet Funding transaction shall use the Visa account supplied to the wallet operator to fund or reimburse the wallet.
A staged digital wallet Purchase transaction shall use the wallet-assigned account context to pay the retailer while retaining the underlying transaction character.
Moneris completion data shall carry the authorization amount and sequence linkage required by the source tables.
The MAC field shall be a fixed 16-character value in both the Moneris request (Table 007) and response (Table 005).
Moneris request tables shall use the source-defined table IDs, fixed lengths, and Moneris terminal/merchant/context values.
Moneris request/response data shall validate MAC, encryption-key indicators, and terminal capability fields according to the Moneris contract.
A Moneris-routed Segment 100 request/response shall include the applicable Moneris Data Segment 135/136.
Moneris Table 006 Sequence Number (10 characters) shall match the Sequence Number used in the corresponding Segment 100 request (Element 86).
Site Language Table ID 001 shall carry a fixed three-digit Table Length of 003 and an ISO 639-2 language code associated with the terminal.
Postal Code Table ID 002 shall carry a fixed three-digit Table Length of 013 and the 13-character international postal code associated with the transmitting device.

A merchant participating in the Online Refund/Refund Authorization program must send the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator in Variable Information Table ID 32 Sub Table 11 on a Merchandise Return transaction requesting online authorization; a merchant not wanting online approval must not send it.
When the Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator is present on a Merchandise Return, it must also be included in the subsequent reversal/follow-up transactions and in Timeout Reversals.
The Online Refund/Refund Authorization Indicator value must be 'Y' for Visa, MasterCard, Amex, and Discover.
Amex SafeKey transactions shall be sent with indicator 'SK' followed by 56 bytes of SafeKey data in base64 format; when the first 28 bytes are not applicable, they shall be space-filled.
A 3-D Secure Authorization Response shall return the applicable ECI/Terminal Type value (25, 26, 27, 28, or 29) together with the card-brand cryptogram: Visa CAVV, MasterCard AAV, or Amex AEVV.

MasterCard AAV cryptogram data shall use Segment 111 Table ID 36 (UCAF Data) while Token/DSRP cryptograms shall use Segment 123 Element 237 (TAVV); when both are present, the UCAF Security Level Code shall be '21' (Channel Encrypted).

For Visa token-based transactions combined with 3-D Secure, the TAVV token cryptogram and the 3DS CAVV cryptogram (revised format) shall be populated per the defined Verified-by-Visa-only, Digital-Wallet-only, or combined scenario.

A cardholder-initiated recurring or installment stored-credential transaction shall use Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'I' and Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'C' (Cardholder Initiated) with the original POS Entry Mode on the initial transaction.
CVV2 data must not be sent for MIT recurring, MIT installment, or CIT recurring/installment stored-credential transactions.
When storing a credential for the first time, Variable Information Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 shall carry Value 'I' (Initial), whether sent as a $0.00 Account Verification or an amount-due transaction.

A merchant-initiated installment stored-credential transaction shall be identified as 'I', use Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'C', POS Entry Mode '10', include Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'M', and must not send CVV2 data.

A merchant-initiated recurring stored-credential transaction shall be identified as 'R', use Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'C' (Subsequent), POS Entry Mode '10', and include Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'M' (Merchant Initiated).

A merchant-initiated unscheduled stored-credential transaction shall not be identified as Installment or Recurring, and shall include Table ID 49 Sub Table 02 = 'M', Table ID 32 Sub Table 08 = 'C', and POS Entry Mode '10'.

The Visa/Amex Transaction ID and Discover Network Reference Number returned on the initial stored-credential authorization response shall be stored and included on all subsequent merchant-initiated transactions using that credential.
